levels.flavorText: Every great empire started with a cart. Yours smells amazing.

units.description: A humble cart on wheels — all empires begin with a single dream and a gas burner.
Corn tortillas, secret salsa, and a queue that wraps around the block.
Hand-pulled, boiling hot, and gone in sixty seconds flat.
Steamed perfection in every bite, and yes, you do need twelve of them.
Crispy, fluffy, sweet — the kind of line that makes adults shove each other politely.

milestones.description: Four and a half stars. The half star is from someone who couldn't find parking.
You're on the neighborhood food map. Strangers now cross town just for your food.

levels.flavorText: Butter, wine, and a maitre d' who definitely judges your shoes.

units.description: Complimentary only in theory — charge by the refill and watch the gold roll in.
Snails in garlic butter — slow to prepare, but guests pay royally for the privilege.
Every dusty bottle is a negotiation. Sommeliers love this. Your accountant loves it more.
Shouting in French makes every dish taste better. A statistical fact.
Red banquettes, jazz, and a prix-fixe menu that justifies the entire renovation.

milestones.description: Michelin says you're excellent value for money. Your regulars already knew that.
One star. It arrives quietly by post, and your reservation list explodes overnight.

levels.flavorText: Nonnas have been perfecting this for centuries. You're just monetizing their genius.

units.description: Bronze-die extruded, hand-cut, and ten minutes from flour to al dente perfection.
Wood-fired at 900°F, Neapolitan certified, and worth every lira.
Cold-pressed liquid gold. Your guests drizzle it on everything, including the dessert.
Prosciutto, salami, and coppa aging in perfect darkness — patience has never tasted this good.
Candlelit tables, cobblestones, and a view that makes every dish taste better.

milestones.description: Denominazione di Origine Protetta — your olive oil is now legally more Italian than anyone else's.
Your trattoria is now a protected culinary treasure. A UNESCO email is probably on the way.

levels.flavorText: Push the trolleys. Fill the bamboo steamers. The palace is always open for one more round.

units.description: Six baskets stacked high with har gow and siu mai — the original meal deal.
Pushed with authority, greeted with joy — the cart that built a thousand Sundays.
Pu-erh, jasmine, oolong — the tea never stops and neither does the conversation.
Lacquered to perfection and carved tableside — the reason every banquet table falls quiet for a moment.
Round tables, lazy susans, and a seating plan that requires a geopolitical negotiation.
Where the recipes are a thousand years old and the chef refuses to write them down.

milestones.description: Three generations of every family arrive at 9am sharp. You've become tradition.
A dish so refined it would have graced the Emperor's table. Your guests feel accordingly regal.

levels.flavorText: Fish freshness is everything. Your suppliers are very, very fast.

units.description: Perfectly seasoned sushi rice is half the art. Your chef treats the cooker like a shrine.
Twenty-four seats, an eight-piece omakase, and a waitlist three months long.
A direct line to the world's finest tuna market. Your fish arrives before sunrise.
A 30-year-old yanagiba and a chef who sharpens it at 5am every morning. Worth every second.
Twelve seats. No menus. The chef decides. Your guests hand over their credit cards with joy.
Each pour chosen to elevate the bite before it. The margin on sake alone is extraordinary.

milestones.description: The fish inspectors have spoken. Your tuna is the most precisely fresh tuna they've ever tasted.
Food writers fly in from three continents. The reservation line is now a philosophical experience.

levels.flavorText: Rules exist to be broken. Flavour combinations exist to be discovered. Your kitchen does both.

units.description: Where turmeric meets truffle and the result is somehow perfect. Science and food, finally together.
Kimchi meets crème fraîche. Your guests can't explain it, but they order it again.
Spherified mango, olive oil snow, edible paper — dinner as theatre, science as flavour.
Ingredients from six continents arranged by flavour profile. Your sous chef needs a map.
A different concept every week, a different city every month, and the same extraordinary food.
Eighteen courses, each a micro-story. Guests come for dinner and leave with a philosophy.

milestones.description: They said it couldn't be done. You did it anyway, and added a foam.
Number forty-three with a bullet. Your name is now mentioned in the same breath as the legends.

levels.flavorText: Three stars. You've arrived. Please don't look at the bill.

units.description: Pressed linen, silver cutlery, and waiting staff who glide. Setting the table costs more than most kitchens cook.
Four bites, complimentary. The psychological ROI is enormous.
Sixty wheels of aged comté and a fromager who speaks to them by name. Madness. Delicious madness.
Decants with authority, serves with ceremony, and costs more than the wine. Worth every euro.
Where perfection isn't a goal, it's the baseline. The pressure is magnificent.
By invitation only. The guest list is classified. The tasting menu is eternal.

milestones.description: Two stars means a detour is worth making. Half your guests now fly in specifically for dinner.
Three stars. Worth a special journey. The Michelin inspectors wept, reportedly unprofessionally.

levels.flavorText: Six continents. Forty restaurants. One name on every reservation list that matters.

units.description: The mothership. Where your story began and where every pilgrim must eventually arrive.
Six hotels, six restaurants, six executive chefs who argue about everything and produce perfection.
Training the next generation to carry your methods. Your legacy now has its own postcode.
A cooking show, a streaming deal, a cookware line, and a perfume for reasons nobody fully understands.
Twelve airlines, four hundred flights daily, and your soufflé somehow still works at 35,000 feet.
The gilded command centre of your empire — from here, a hundred kitchens take orders from one table.

milestones.description: Your logo is on hats now. Strange but profitable. There is no going back.
UNESCO declared your tasting menu an intangible cultural treasure. The waiting list is measured in decades.

characters.quote: Every great chef started by burning something. I just made it a business model.
Butter is not a condiment. It is a philosophy.
I never measure anything. The pasta knows.
A dim sum morning is a happy morning. Everything else is consequences.
The fish tells you what shape it wants to become. My job is to listen.
I source better than I sleep. Both are impressive.
I once made a dessert out of nostalgia and smoked caramel. Both were on the menu.
My pantry speaks twelve languages. My cooking is the translation.
Excellence is not a mood. It is a policy.
I built an empire one recipe at a time. The accountants are still catching up.
